tracks.name: Dover Motor Speedway
tracks.dfsLeanNote: Dominators strongly favored. Track position is nearly everything here — the high-banked concrete makes passing brutally hard. Elite cars up front stay there and lap leaders rack up massive DK points.
keyPatterns: Laps led are highly concentrated — typically 2-4 drivers account for 300+ of 400 laps
Winners almost always start top 10; deep PD charges are rare without major attrition
Hard on tires and equipment — late-race cautions are common, which can shuffle the field
Concrete surface = less tire falloff than asphalt, rewards consistent speed over tire management

dfsStrategy.cash: Stack the clear dominator. At Dover, one driver often leads 100+ laps — that's 25+ DK pts from laps led alone. Don't fade the chalk here; just make sure you own enough of the dominator.
dfsStrategy.gpp: Dominator-first build still applies. Look for secondary dominators at mid-range salary to differentiate. PD plays can work for value roster spots but don't anchor a GPP around them — the upside ceiling is too low relative to a 100-lap leader.

tracks.pdNotes: PD is mostly a bonus, not a strategy. Best PD spot is a highly-rated driver who qualifies poorly (15-25th) and runs clean — think Larson in 2024 (+19 spots, 2nd place). But even that play had 39 laps led layered in. Pure PD with 0 laps led rarely scores well enough at Dover.

formatNotes.note: Special 3-segment format: 75 laps (Seg 1) + 75 laps (Seg 2, inverted top-26 from Seg 1) + 200 laps (Seg 3, top 26 drivers only). 19 drivers locked into Seg 3 automatically; remaining spots filled by combined Seg 1+2 performance. Non-locked drivers are GPP-only — too much variance to use in cash. DK uses overall qualifying grid for PD, not segment restart positions.

historicalWinners.note: Led 136 of 400 laps, held off Larson by 0.256s
One of the rare mid-pack-to-win results at Dover

keyDriversToWatch.note: The Dover king. Historically dominant — expect 80%+ pLL projections when healthy. Low ownership relative to talent is a recurring theme.
Strong Dover car but tends to be overrostered. Watch ownership vs. his pLL gap.
Historically strong here, though now retired (2024).

fadeList: Drivers starting outside top 25 with no historical Dover speed
Road course specialists — concrete ovals are a completely different skill set
Anyone with 35%+ ownership and <10% pLL (classic All-Star Race trap: Preece, SVG in 2026)

tracks.name: Watkins Glen International
tracks.dfsLeanNote: Road courses skew chalk. Front-runners dominate because track position is hard to overcome — only 2 winners from outside top 10 in the last decade at The Glen. Cash strategies work well; contrarian GPP edges are smaller than at ovals.
keyPatterns: Track position matters more than at most ovals — limited passing zones
Only 2 winners from outside top 10 in the last decade
Road course specialists (SVG, Montoya guests) can spike ownership — analyze if the pace actually backs it up
Pit strategy can create massive position swings — track position after pit cycles is a major DK score driver
Weather matters more than at ovals — rain brings massive chaos and randomness

dfsStrategy.cash: Play the fastest cars that also qualify well. Fade road course 'specialists' if their ownership is spiked beyond their realistic finishing range. Keep 1-2 mid-tier drivers who have shown Glen pace before.
dfsStrategy.gpp: Harder to differentiate at road courses. Look for elite drivers who qualify poorly due to strategy or issues — they'll have PD upside plus potential to make a run. Pit strategy chaos can create massive point swings.

tracks.pdNotes: PD is more viable here than at Dover but still secondary to finishing position and laps led. Pit strategy-driven PD (driver pits under green, gets track position) is the most common mechanism. Deep-field PD charges from 25+ back are still rare.

historicalWinners.note: SVG's Cup debut win — the road course specialist effect

keyDriversToWatch.note: Elite road course driver, historically dominant at The Glen.
Road course specialist — big ownership spikes. Must verify if pace data backs it up at each specific course.
Consistent road course performer, often underrated.

fadeList: Pure oval specialists with no road course results
Any 'specialist' driver with 35%+ ownership but only 5-10 laps led upside — the ownership premium eats into value
